title: Preparation of Tissue for Ribo-Tag/RNAseq Analysis
author: Cecilia Tubert
materials: Optional: repeat saline injection to prevent dehydration
Right before the procedure, prepare fresh slicing solution.
Terminally anesthetize the mouse according to institutional protocols.
Proceed with other tubes one by one

steps.title: Prepare Post-Operative and Working Environment
steps.instruction: Set up the surgical and recovery areas to ensure sterility and temperature control.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a clean empty mouse cage on a heating pad.
Prepare a clean mouse cage with gel food for post-operative care.
Set up a sterile working area including a stereotaxic frame.

steps.title: Anesthetize and Position Mouse
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse and secure it onto the stereotaxic frame while maintaining body temperature.

substeps.instruction: Measure the weight of the mouse.
Anesthetize mouse in induction chamber (recommended: 2.5% isoflurane, 200ml/min flow rate).
Clip hair over the surgery area.
Once deeply anesthetized (~5 min), stop anesthesia and move the mouse to the stereotaxic frame over a heating pad with a temperature probe; secure the mouth on the nose cone.
Restart anesthesia directed towards the nose cone.
Adjust heating pad so the temperature probe reads a body temperature between 33-37°C.
Apply ophthalmic ointment over eyes.

steps.title: Administer Analgesics and Secure Head
steps.instruction: Provide pain relief and stabilize the mouse head for precise coordinates.

substeps.instruction: Inject appropriate volume of analgesic based on mouse weight and desired dosage; inject saline if needed to prevent dehydration.
Carefully insert and secure ear-bars, ensuring the head is not visibly tilted.

steps.title: Expose the Skull
steps.instruction: Sterilize the incision site and expose the skull.

substeps.instruction: Clean the incision area with a povidone-iodine swab followed by an ethanol swab; repeat 3 times.
Apply line-block anesthetic (0.15% bupivacaine) under the skull skin.
Make an anterior-posterior incision with fine scissors to expose the skull.

steps.title: Determine Injection Coordinates
steps.instruction: Locate anatomical landmarks and calculate the specific injection site.

substeps.instruction: Insert a glass pipette (optionally using non-toxic food dye) on the stereotaxic arm holder and lower it onto the skull.
Mark bregma by touching the intersection of coronal/sagittal sutures and zero the coordinates.
Move to lambda (intersection of lambdoid and sagittal sutures) and measure its position relative to bregma.
Adjust head position to minimize dorso/ventral (D/V) and medio/lateral (M/L) deviation between lambda and bregma.
Re-zero coordinates at bregma and repeat measurements until satisfactory.

Calculate an adjustment factor by dividing the measured bregma-lambda (B-L) distance by the reference distance of 4.21; multiply reference coordinates by this ratio if the mouse is smaller than average.
Move the pipette to the adjusted A/P and M/L coordinates and mark the spot.
For bi-lateral injections, mark both sides and minimize relative D/V deviation by adjusting the head.

steps.title: Perform Viral Injection
steps.instruction: Drill the skull and deliver the viral solution into the brain tissue.

substeps.instruction: Remove the marker pipette and drill a hole in the skull at the indicated position.
Clean blood and debris with sterile saline and sterile cotton swabs.
Insert a micropipette with volumetric references into the holder and connect to a syringe.
Draw the desired volume of viral solution into the syringe using negative pressure.
Lower the pipette into the hole until the tip touches the dura and zero the D/V coordinate.
Gradually lower the pipette tip into the brain to the desired D/V coordinate.
Slowly inject the viral solution (recommended: ~150/200nl/min) using gradual positive pressure.
Release pressure and leave the pipette in position for ~5-10min for absorption.

steps.title: Post-Surgical Recovery and Monitoring
steps.instruction: Recover the animal and provide follow-up care.

substeps.instruction: Remove animal from frame and place in the clean empty cage on a heating pad until deambulatory (~10-15min).
Move the awake mouse to the clean cage with gel food on a heating pad.
Administer a second dose of Metacam and apply antibiotic ointment to sutured skin 24 hours after surgery.
Monitor health status; administer additional Metacam or saline if needed.
Keep mouse in a cage on a heating pad for at least 4 days before moving to standard housing.
Sacrifice mice for tissue collection 4 weeks after surgeries.

steps.title: Prepare Slicing and Perfusion Equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare ice-cold solutions and the vibratome for tissue processing.

substeps.instruction: Prepare ~200ml of slicing solution (freeze it or keep at 4°C) and pre-chill fresh aCSF at 4°C.
Create a 'slushie' by mixing pre-frozen slicing solution with freshly-made solution using an immersion blender.
Set up a recirculating system: bubble the slushie and run it through a peristaltic pump with a needle returning the solution to the slushie.
Pour cold aCSF into a holding chamber, place on ice, and keep under continuous bubbling.
Fill two large trays with ice: one with an inclined area for perfusion and one with an upside-down petri dish covered with filter paper (with another empty dish dug into the ice for slushie).
Pre-chill dissection tools in ice.
Place razor blades, a 0.5x0.5in agar block, and the vibratome holding stage on a precision wipe over ice.
Turn on vibratome and set parameters (for midbrain coronal: 220um thickness, 0.06 mm/s speed, 1mm oscillation amplitude).
Perform vibration check with the vibro-check tool and double-edge blade; minimize vibration and remove the tool.
Place the slicing chamber in the vibratome ice tray and fill surrounding areas with ice.
Prepare dissection area with a microscope, petri dish, pre-chilled tools, scalpels, and a container of dry ice or liquid nitrogen.
Pre-chill Eppendorf tubes on ice.

steps.title: Perform Transcardiac Perfusion
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse and perfuse the brain with ice-cold slicing solution.

substeps.instruction: Verify full anesthesia via paw-pinch reflex.
Position mouse supine with head facing downward (if inclined) and secure paws with needles.
Cut skin below the sternum to expose the peritoneal cavity and rib cage; cut the fascia connecting skin to rib cage.
Carefully cut the diaphragm and chest cage, lifting the cage toward the head.
Insert the needle connected to the recirculating slicing solution slushie into the left ventricle and pinch the right atrium with spring scissors.
Allow solution to wash out blood until the liver looks pale (typically 10-20s).
Remove the needle and quickly decapitate the mouse.

steps.title: Extract and Prepare Brain for Slicing
steps.instruction: Remove the brain from the skull and mount it on the vibratome stage.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the head into a petri dish filled with slicing slushie.

Cut the skin to expose the skull median line; remove the posterior skull, then cut along the median line rostrally, making diagonal cuts toward the eyes and later cuts along lambdoidal sutures, keeping the head cold.
Open the skull with tweezers and gently remove the brain with a spatula, sliding it into the slicing slushie.
Wet the filter paper of the second petri dish with slicing slushie.
Wipe the vibratome holding stage dry and apply super glue to the center.
Move the brain to the filter paper; use a single-edge blade to remove the rostral striatum and cerebellum (for midbrain coronal slices).
Move the brain to the glue on the holding stage (frontal part facing down) and place the agarose block on the dorsal part of the brain.
Insert the holding stage into the slicing chamber (ventral brain facing blade, agarose facing operator).
Pour slicing slushie into the chamber to cover the brain, add a bubbler, and gently move residual ice toward the operator to leave the brain visible.

steps.title: Slice and Collect Tissue
steps.instruction: Slice the brain and dissect the specific region of interest.

substeps.instruction: Lower the blade, adjust inclination, set slicing cycle, and manually position the blade near the start region.
Discard undesired fragments until the region of interest is reached.
Immediately transfer slices of interest into the holding chamber or directly to the dissection petri dish.
Transfer slices one by one to the dissection petri dish and dissect the area of interest under a microscope.
Collect tissue of interest in a pre-chilled tube with minimal solution volume.
Label the tube and quickly freeze it in dry ice or liquid nitrogen.
Collect a tail fragment for genotyping if required.
Dispose of carcass and sharps according to guidelines; store frozen samples at -80°C.

steps.title: Isolate RNA via Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Homogenize tissue and use sequential magnetic bead captures to isolate target RNA.

substeps.instruction: Transfer frozen samples from -80°C to dry ice.
Place sample on ice, add 100ul pre-chilled tissue homogenization solution, homogenize, then add 700ul more homogenization solution.
Centrifuge at 4°C for 10 min at 12,000g.
Transfer supernatant to new pre-chilled tubes and add 40ul pre-washed Pierce Protein A/G Magnetic Beads.
Rotate gently at 4°C for 1 hour.
Collect beads with a chilled magnet, transfer supernatant to new pre-chilled tubes, and add 40ul pre-washed Anti-Flag Magnetic Beads.
Rotate gently at 4°C for 16-18 h.
Collect beads with a magnet and resuspend in 800ul washing buffer; rotate gently at 4°C for 15-20 min.
Repeat the wash step three times.
Resuspend beads in 300ul RLT Lyses buffer (RNAeasy Micro kit) at room temperature, vortex, and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove beads with a magnet and perform RNA purification following the kit manufacturer's instructions.
Transfer samples to NUseq core for RNAseq analysis.
